headline: The water bottle slipped out at 8.6 s: 2.7 N of grip for a load that needs 4.4 N, after grip_effort was cut to 0.28.

claims.text: The tray holds nothing; the water bottle is not in it.

At 8.60 s, during 'picking up the water bottle', the fingers closed from 48 to 0 deg on a closed command, grip current fell from 0.28 to 0.09 A, and the camera saw the water bottle 42 cm away from the fingertip.
The gripper squeezed with 2.7 N; holding a 0.45 kg water bottle still needs 4.4 N. It could not have held it once lifted.
grip_effort was cut from 0.6 to 0.28 on 2026-10-09: "grip_effort 0.6 -> 0.28 so the gripper stops crushing paper cups (PR #212)."
The run ran out of time. Refuted: the run ended at 22.00 s, inside its 25 s deadline.
The arm hit something. Refuted: no joint ever stalled against its command; the largest tracking error was 2.0 deg on the wrist_flex.
The arm moved a different object than the goal named. Refuted: the grasped object is the water bottle (0.97), the goal's target.
The gripper closed on nothing. Refuted: every grasp stopped on an object.
The arm accelerated too hard while carrying. Refuted: peak acceleration before the slip was 0.4 m/s^2, under the 2.5 m/s^2 carry limit.
Worn finger pads lost their friction. Refuted: the pads have 214 of 1500 rated cycles; they are nearly new.
Revert grip_effort to its default for heavy items; keep the low setting only for objects flagged fragile.

hypotheses.test: Where the camera last saw every object labelled as the target, and whether that is inside the destination zone.
hypotheses.refute_if: No object labelled as the target is inside the destination zone in the last camera frame.
hypotheses.summary: The tray holds nothing; the water bottle is not in it.
hypotheses.why: decides whether there is a failure to explain

hypotheses.statement: The run ran out of time.
hypotheses.test: Whether the controller hit the goal's deadline before finishing.
hypotheses.refute_if: The run ended before the deadline with no deadline event.
hypotheses.summary: The run ended at 22.00 s, inside its 25 s deadline.

hypotheses.test: Whether a joint stalled (measured speed near zero) while its command kept moving, building tracking error, and whether its motor current rose with it. Lag at high speed builds error too, but the joint keeps moving.
hypotheses.refute_if: No joint stalls with more than 2.5 deg of tracking error while its command is moving.
hypotheses.summary: No joint ever stalled against its command; the largest tracking error was 2.0 deg on the wrist_flex.

hypotheses.statement: The object slipped out of the gripper.
hypotheses.test: After the grasp, whether the fingers (still commanded closed) closed past the object, and whether the object's camera track fell away from the fingertip.
hypotheses.refute_if: The gripper opening stays at the object's width from the grasp until the gripper is commanded open.
hypotheses.summary: At 8.60 s, during 'picking up the water bottle', the fingers closed from 48 to 0 deg on a closed command, grip current fell from 0.28 to 0.09 A, and the camera saw the water bottle 42 cm away from the fingertip.

runs.summary: The gripper held the object at 35.0 deg from 5.84 s until it was told to open at 12.40 s.

hypotheses.statement: The arm moved a different object than the goal named.
hypotheses.test: Which camera track was in the fingers at the grasp, and what perception called it at close range.
hypotheses.refute_if: The grasped track's confident label is the goal's target.
hypotheses.summary: The grasped object is the water bottle (0.97), the goal's target.

hypotheses.test: Whether a grasp closed the fingers fully (below 3 deg) right after reaching for the object.
hypotheses.refute_if: Every grasp stopped on an object (opening above 3 deg).
hypotheses.summary: Every grasp stopped on an object.

hypotheses.statement: Grip force was too low for the object's weight.
hypotheses.test: Grip force from the gripper motor current while holding, against the force needed to hold the object's catalogued weight at rest: m g / (2 mu).
hypotheses.refute_if: Grip force is at least the static requirement.
hypotheses.summary: The gripper squeezed with 2.7 N; holding a 0.45 kg water bottle still needs 4.4 N. It could not have held it once lifted.

hypotheses.statement: The arm accelerated too hard while carrying.
hypotheses.test: Peak fingertip acceleration in the 0.5 s before the slip, against the controller's carry limit and the acceleration this grip can withstand: 2 mu F / m - g.
hypotheses.refute_if: Peak acceleration before the slip stays under config.max_carry_accel.
hypotheses.summary: Peak acceleration before the slip was 0.4 m/s^2, under the 2.5 m/s^2 carry limit.

hypotheses.statement: A config change lowered the grip.
hypotheses.test: config.grip_effort against its default, and the changelog entry that set it.
hypotheses.refute_if: grip_effort is at its default, or no changelog entry changed it.
hypotheses.summary: grip_effort was cut from 0.6 to 0.28 on 2026-10-09: "grip_effort 0.6 -> 0.28 so the gripper stops crushing paper cups (PR #212)."

hypotheses.statement: Worn finger pads lost their friction.
hypotheses.test: Grasp cycles on the finger pads since replacement, against their rated life, from the maintenance log.
hypotheses.refute_if: The pads are within their rated cycles.
hypotheses.summary: The pads have 214 of 1500 rated cycles; they are nearly new.
